notes: Verified live 21-Aug-2026 (architecture review), RE-verified live again 21-Aug-2026 (Phase 3 build, same day) via a fresh browser session — the table structure (id=example1, column order Flag/Unit/Code/Currency/We Buy/We Sell/Last Updated) is unchanged from the original inspection, unlike My Money Master which had drifted. The raw HTTP response's <tbody> is empty (headers only) — the rows are filled in by client-side JavaScript that calls an internal API (https://fx.tajmuhabath.com.my/rbapi/WebRbService.svc/json/getdailyratesapi) AFTER the page loads. That internal API was inspected via the browser's network log during this re-verification and confirmed to require an authorization the page's own JS supplies (an unauthenticated call to it returns {"appError":{"ErrCode":-104,"ErrMsg":"user not authorized to access.!"}}) — this adapter deliberately does NOT attempt to call that API directly or replicate whatever token/session unlocks it, since doing so would mean working around an access control, which this project's compliance rules (and this assistant's operating rules) prohibit. Playwright browser automation against the public page, exactly as the project brief anticipated for this site, is the only extraction path used.
requiresBrowserAutomationReason: Confirmed live: a raw HTTP GET of liveRateUrl returns table#example1 with zero <tbody><tr> rows — every currency row (including CNY) is populated by client-side JS after page load, staggered roughly 1-2 seconds apart per row. A plain HTTP fetch + HTML parse cannot see this data at all; there is no non-Playwright primary path for this site (unlike My Money Master).
playwrightFallbackReason: Playwright IS the primary (and only) path here, not a fallback — there is nothing simpler to fall back FROM.
branchNotes: A native <select id="dpdBranch"> offers branch selection. Its <option> VALUES are opaque numeric branch IDs (e.g. "17", "18") that are not human-meaningful and could be reassigned by the site at any time — select by the option's visible TEXT LABEL instead (e.g. "LALAPORT BBCC"), via Playwright's page.selectOption({ label }). The page loads with a default branch already selected ("THE EXCHANGE TRX" as of this verification) — if no branch is requested, the adapter reads whatever branch loaded by default and reports that branch's name in the result, rather than silently reading an arbitrary/undocumented default.
knownBranchesObservedAt: 2026-08-21 (Phase 3 live re-verification) — this list is informational only (for UI dropdowns / sanity checks), not authoritative; the adapter should always read the live <option> list from the page rather than hardcoding against this array for extraction purposes.

primarySelector.description: table#example1's has one per currency (26 observed). Cell order per row: [0] flag , [1] Unit (e.g. "1" or, for CNY specifically, "100" — CNY's Buy/Sell figures are per 100 units of CNY, not per 1, which is why they look numerically similar in scale to My Money Master's per-1-unit-implied CNY figures; both sites are internally consistent with each other on this so target-rate comparisons between the two sources remain apples-to-apples), [2] Code (ISO-ish code, e.g. "CNY", "USD-S"), [3] Currency display name (visually hidden column, still present in DOM), [4] We Buy, [5] We Sell, [6] Last Updated (visually hidden column, still present in DOM, format "DD-MM-YYYY hh:mm:ss AM/PM").
primarySelector.matchStrategy: Enumerate table#example1 tbody tr rows, find the one whose codeCellIndex cell's trimmed text exactly equals the requested ISO currency code (e.g. "CNY") — NOT the display-name column, unlike My Money Master which keys by display name. Read buyCellIndex/sellCellIndex as the numeric Buy/Sell values, and lastUpdatedCellIndex as the row's own sourceTimestamp (parse "DD-MM-YYYY hh:mm:ss AM/PM" — do not assume a browser-locale-dependent Date.parse() will handle this format correctly; parse it explicitly).

waitStrategy.initialLoad: navigate to liveRateUrl, wait for table#example1 tbody tr to have at least 1 row, THEN wait an additional short settle window (recommend 3-5s) before reading — rows populate progressively (observed ~1-2s apart per row on initial load) and a naive 'table visible = data ready' check can read a row before its value/timestamp cells are filled in.
waitStrategy.afterBranchChange: If a non-default branch is requested: use page.selectOption('#dpdBranch', { label: branchName }) — NOT a synthetic DOM 'change' event (confirmed during live verification that a scripted/untrusted change event does not reliably trigger the site's own branch-reload handler; Playwright's selectOption dispatches a proper trusted browser-level interaction, which does). After selecting, wait for the same settle window as initialLoad before reading, since the branch change triggers a fresh authenticated fetch of that branch's rates.

validation.notes: Same scale/reasoning as My Money Master's CNY range (per-100-unit CNY quoted against MYR). Reject a reading where buyRate > sellRate, or where the value looks like it's missing the /100 unit scaling. USD/SGD/GBP/EUR/AUD/HKD/THB/TWD/JPY/KRW/VND ranges added 26-Aug-2026 (Phase 38), built around the real values observed live that same day (see primarySelector's Phase 38 note), generous padding matching this file's existing CNY convention. Unlike mymoneymaster.json/merchantradeasia.json, this source is code-matched — it did not require any currencyDisplayNames change to make these 11 currencies checkable; the adapter already worked for any code the live table lists. These expectedRange entries exist purely as this file's own sanity-bound layer, matching the other 3 sources' convention, not because the adapter needed them to function.
validation.sourceTimestampStalenessNote: This site (unlike My Money Master) exposes a genuine per-row 'Last Updated' timestamp, which can legitimately be hours old for a currency whose rate simply hasn't moved recently — this is normal market behavior, not a broken scrape. The adapter treats a reading as LIVE if it was successfully retrieved and passed validateRate(), and separately flags it STALE (informationally, in the result's status) only if sourceTimestamp is older than a generous threshold (see backend/scrapers/tajmuhabath.adapter.js STALENESS_THRESHOLD_MS) — this threshold is a judgment call made without strong evidence of what 'too old' means for this specific currency pair's real trading frequency, and is easy to tune later once real historical data accumulates.
